learning_outcomes.text: Providing the fundamental knowledge of the models, languages and technologies for requirements specification, design, implementation, testing, deployment and maintenance of software systems.
The lectures will provide the students with the ability to know and understand the major technology, scientific and application-related trends in the software engineering.

Through laboratory practical classes the students will describe the specific requirements and design of a software system. The students will be able to design software according to patterns consolidated and available in the literature.
The students will be able to assess whether a program has been specified, designed and developed in compliance with well-known, standard quality methodologies.
The studentd will be able to gather and describe the technical specifications of a software.
The student will achieve the knowledge and the ability to perform further and complete investigations on the issues of software design.

syllabus_topics: Requirement specifications
Using the UML use case diagram for the representation of the requirements
Design
High-level design definition and detail
Examples of architectural styles
Functional decomposition
Object Relational Mapping: definition and issues
Defining the design quality characteristics
Introduction of metrics for software evaluation
Definition of cohesion and coupling of software modules
Use of UML diagrams for the description of the software
ORM: JPA and Hibernate
Use of design patterns for software design
Implementation, testing
Defining what it is meant by good planning and identification of best practices
Software refactoring
Software testing and code inspection
Survey of several testing techniques (Path Analysis, Boundary values analysis, ...)
Junit: the framework for testing Java programs
Overview of basic techniques of defensive programming
Maven and Git programming support, and software management
Distribution and Maintenance
Description of the main problems associated with configuration management and post-production software
Types of software licenses
AI-Native Software Engineering
Use of LLMs and agents across the different phases of the software development lifecycle
Opportunities, limitations, and risks of AI-generated code
The role of human verification
Demonstration of AI coding assistants for software generation, comprehension, modification, refactoring, and testing

assessment_methods.method: Written test: exercises for software application design (use case diagrams, class diagrams, sequence diagrams, package diagrams, activity diagrams, design patterns)
Written test: testing exercises (identifying tests to perform for a given function)
Individual report describing a software product (requirements, UML diagrams, design patterns)

assessment_rules: Learning is verified through a written test and a report. The written test consists of 3-4 open questions (30% of overall evaluation), software application design exercises (55% of overall evaluation), and testing exercises (55% of overall evaluation). The individual report describes a software product in detail, assessed on precision and correctness (25%), completeness in design and use of patterns (50%), and "wow effect" (25%).

Martin Fowler, UML Distilled: A Brief Guide to the Standard Object Modeling Language , Pearson Addison Wesley
Martina Seidl, Marion Scholz, Christian Huemer, Gerti Kappel: UML @ Classroom - An Introduction to Object-Oriented Modeling, Springer 2015
